# Jonas's Morning Pulse
*Sat, Mar 14, 18:00 → Sun, Mar 15, 07:00*

## Cyber Security

### [Microsoft releases out-of-band Windows 11 patch for RRAS RCE vulnerability](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/microsoft-releases-windows-11-oob-hotpatch-to-fix-rras-rce-flaw/)
*Mar 14, 22:48*

Microsoft issued an emergency patch for Windows 11 Enterprise systems to fix a remote code execution flaw in Routing and Remote Access Service. The OOB update targets environments using hotpatch delivery instead of regular Patch Tuesday cycles. This represents a critical vulnerability requiring immediate attention given Microsoft's decision to break from normal patching cadence.

> *Emergency patches signal severe risk; assess enterprise exposure to RRAS and hotpatch deployment timelines*

Sources: [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/microsoft-releases-windows-11-oob-hotpatch-to-fix-rras-rce-flaw/)

## AI & Machine Learning

### [AI-generated spam forces Jazzband to abandon open-source collaboration model](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Mar/14/jannis-leidel/#atom-everything)
*Mar 14, 19:41*

GitHub's flood of AI-generated spam PRs has made open membership models untenable for projects like Jazzband. Only 1 in 10 AI-generated PRs now meet project standards, and curl shut down its bug bounty after confirmation rates dropped below 5%. GitHub's response included a kill switch to disable pull requests entirely. This represents a fundamental shift in how open-source projects must manage AI-generated contributions.

> *Shows how AI spam is breaking traditional open-source trust models, relevant for any enterprise using or contributing to OSS*

Sources: [Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Mar/14/jannis-leidel/#atom-everything)

### [Developer adoption of AI coding tools reaches 'nobody reads code' stage](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Mar/14/pragmatic-summit/#atom-everything)
*Mar 14, 19:19*

Simon Willison discusses evolution of AI adoption in software development, highlighting StrongDM's controversial 'software factory' approach where developers neither write nor read code. The progression moves from ChatGPT queries to coding agents writing more code than humans, with trust models shifting to treat AI like external team dependencies. StrongDM, a security company, claims to build serious software without human code review.

> *Critical inflection point for enterprise development practices and security oversight models as AI becomes primary code author*

Sources: [Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Mar/14/pragmatic-summit/#atom-everything)

## Technology

### [Apple's MacBook Neo becomes most repairable MacBook in 14 years](https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/14/the-macbook-neo-is-the-most-repairable-macbook-in-years-according-to-ifixit/)
*Mar 14, 22:24*

iFixit declares Apple's new affordable MacBook Neo the company's most repairable laptop in over a decade. This marks a significant departure from Apple's historical approach to device repairability and suggests potential compliance with right-to-repair regulations.

> *Signals broader industry shift toward repairability requirements that may affect enterprise hardware procurement and lifecycle management*

Sources: [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/14/the-macbook-neo-is-the-most-repairable-macbook-in-years-according-to-ifixit/)

## Business & Markets

### [US Army awards Anduril up to $20B contract consolidating 120+ procurement actions](https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/14/us-army-announces-contract-with-anduril-worth-up-to-20b/)
*Mar 14, 21:47*

The Army announced a massive single enterprise contract with defense tech startup Anduril worth up to $20 billion. The deal consolidates more than 120 separate procurement actions into one comprehensive agreement, representing a significant shift toward streamlined defense technology acquisition.

> *Shows how defense sector is embracing startup tech providers with enterprise-scale contracts, potential model for other sectors*

Sources: [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/14/us-army-announces-contract-with-anduril-worth-up-to-20b/)

### [Honda abandons three US EV models, retreats from electric vehicle market](https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/14/honda-is-killing-its-evs-and-any-chance-of-competing-in-the-future/)
*Mar 14, 18:23*

Honda is killing its three electric vehicles designed for the US market, effectively withdrawing from EV competition. The decision will impact Honda's position beyond North America as the automotive industry rapidly shifts toward electrification. This represents a major strategic retreat by a traditional automaker.

> *Illustrates how established companies can miscalculate technology transitions, relevant for enterprise digital transformation strategy*

Sources: [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/14/honda-is-killing-its-evs-and-any-chance-of-competing-in-the-future/)
